note: Measurements present in the pre-compression revision and absent from both main.tex and the generated appendix afterwards.  Each entry's tokens are verified against the old revision at the recorded line numbers, so this appendix cannot introduce a number that was not already measured; and against the built PDF, so it cannot be silently truncated.

restored.title: Defect (8): the corrected denominator, in full
restored.why: This is the derivation of the $2.95\sigma$ that Appendix~\ref{app:derivations} quotes as a bare constant when it argues that a mis-pairing control reaches a minimum of $0.3\sigma$.  Without it the reader has no way to know that $2.95\sigma$ is a \emph{pass} under the corrected gate and a fail under the pre-registered one, which is the whole content of ledger row (8).

restored.title: The two margins closest to the propagated noise floor
restored.why: Table~\ref{tab:e11b}'s caption states the conclusion---that the replicate-averaged re-measurement changes the median margin ``by less than $1.4\%$''---but the compression deleted the two margins the conclusion is about.  They are the smallest in the table ($-3.03$ on task 900049 and $-3.53$ on 900053), i.e.\ the two the $5\times$ pre-registered bar could plausibly have been breached on, so they are the only two a reader would want to see move.

restored.title: Solver quality behind the assignment-block ranking
restored.why: These qualify the $\rho = 0.518$ / sign $0.756$ over 12 designs that \S\ref{sec:relax} quotes from the superseded E0 record for the \textbf{assignment} block---the block E13 later measured at $\rho = 0.166$ and E14 at $1/8$.  A rank correlation computed after 238 line-search rescues and 5 skipped edits is not the same measurement as one from a clean solve, and the body quotes the correlation without them.

restored.title: The counter-measurement that withdrew the pixel-separability claim
restored.why: \S\ref{sec:related} withdraws the sentence asserting that a wrong camera ``moves more than $1\%$ of pixels by more than $64/255$'' and quotes only the $0.025\%$.  The point of the withdrawal is that the \emph{claimed} separation was two orders of magnitude and the \emph{measured} one is not, and that argument needs both thresholds, not one.

restored.title: $ 9$ was true only of the printed plate
restored.why: Figure~\ref{fig:containment}'s caption now quotes $11/255$ alone.  The self-correction matters because the two numbers come from two different renders of the same scene, and a determinism bar stated against the smaller one is a different bar from the same bar stated against the larger one.  This is ledger row (25)'s ``a number quoted from prose rather than from a record''.

restored.title: The raster's own exceedance fraction, frac\_gt\_1
restored.why: Appendix~\ref{sec:figures} reports the ``more than $\pm1$ LSB'' finding as a max channel difference only.  The fraction is what makes $8$--$13$ levels benign rather than alarming: it is the fraction of pixels differing by more than one level, and at $8.3\times10^{-3}$ it says the difference is spread thin.  A max with no fraction cannot distinguish antialiasing from a moved object.

restored.title: The separation the bar is actually shown to achieve
restored.why: \S\ref{sec:related} keeps the $14\times$ and drops the $4\times$.  Reporting only the larger of two factors measuring one separation is the same move as reporting only the favourable noise floor, which \S\ref{sec:search} explicitly refuses to do (``quoting only the favourable one is how a $5\times$ bar becomes decorative'').

restored.title: The compiled-project size triple behind ``273--318\,KB''
restored.why: \S\ref{sec:intro} quotes the rounded range 273--318\,KB and the count.  The triple is the evidence, and the review that found the loss re-measured it independently: $2213$ files exactly ($2165$ under its scratch directory plus $48$ in the repository), and over the $1797$ non-stub projects a minimum of $272.8877$\,KB, median $287.18$, maximum $317.3828$, with $368$ sub-$100$\,KB stubs excluded.  An earlier draft said ``90--320\,KB'', taking the lower bound from plan prose.

restored.title: The critical value the $$ derivation hard-codes
restored.why: Appendix~\ref{app:derivations} now says only that the script ``hard-codes $z = 1.96$''.  The whole finding is that this choice is doing the work---at $t(7)$ the pooled inverse cluster interval \emph{contains} $133.7$---and the reader cannot assess that without knowing what $1.96$ was justified by and why the justification does not transfer to $8$ clusters.

restored.title: The two-sample caveat every floor ratio inherits
restored.why: \S\ref{sec:env} states the two noise floors ($0.043$\,K and $0.0168$ for the uncontained room) and \S\ref{sec:search} divides six measured effects by them.  That $n = 2$ is the sample size behind a denominator used in every significance claim in the paper is the single most load-bearing caveat in it, and the compression deleted the sentence that says so.

restored.title: Why $$ was pre-registered rather than fitted
restored.why: Appendix~\ref{app:derivations} says $\lambda$ was ``fixed before this run'' without saying what the alternative was.  The pilot is the reason the weight is a pre-registration at all: at $\lambda = 1$ the liquid term dominates so completely that the air objective---the expensive one, the one this paper exists to differentiate---does not affect the ranking.  Pre-registering $\lambda$ is what makes the $\lambda$-sweep in \S\ref{sec:search} descriptive rather than a search.

restored.title: The evidence that three decision blocks are constant
restored.why: \S\ref{sec:search}'s limit (b) is the paper's most consequential scope restriction: the environment defines seven decision blocks and the search has only ever moved two.  The parenthetical is what makes ``constant'' a measurement rather than an impression---it names the fields read out of the records and the values found.

restored.title: The de-biasing was not itself an optimisation
restored.why: The de-biasing recovered each arm's \emph{selected} design from its archived compiled project rather than replaying the search, and evaluated each three more times.  The minimum-over-$24$ selection bias is therefore removed by construction: no arm gets to re-choose a design against the fresh draws.  Without this sentence a reader cannot tell that re-measurement from a re-run, and a re-run \emph{would} be an artifact of minimising over noise.

restored.title: Defect (9): the gate that passed over degenerate labels
restored.why: Ledger row (9) and \S\ref{sec:lessons} both say the generator implemented neither half of the pre-registered action-space restriction, but neither says what the gate did about it: it exited $0$.  ``48 identical degenerate labels'' is the count, and it is the whole dataset.  This is the campaign's ``a check whose denominator can be zero passed on zero'' pattern in its clearest instance.

restored.title: Defect (22) was reproduced, not asserted
restored.why: The vacuous pass---$24$ strictly-winning records plus $6$ empty ones scoring $24/24$, $p = 0.0$, gate passed---was reproduced from synthetic records before it was fixed, and the fix was then verified against the pre-fix scorer, which returns the vacuous pass identically with and without \texttt{--allow-unequal}.  A defect that is only argued is not a defect that was found.

restored.title: The room shell was never made translucent
restored.why: Every 3-D figure in this paper comes from the simulator's own web frontend, so what the renderer does and does not draw is a property of the evidence.  \S\ref{sec:related} says only ``the shell was never actually made translucent''; the mechanism---a five-alternative regex matching no mesh, and the flag that was passed but never took effect---is what makes that a diagnosis rather than an observation, and it is why the frontend's blindness to containment baffles (defect (11)) was not caught by looking at a plate.

covered_elsewhere.what: the bootstrap median of $\lambda$'s own interval, $129.7$
covered_elsewhere.note: Lost from main.tex by the compression and reported lost from the generated appendix too, at the revision under review.  It is back: \texttt{fill\_results.py} regenerates the $\lambda$-conditioning table from the record on every build, and that table now carries the \texttt{bootstrap\_median} row.  Restoring it by hand here would create two copies of one number, and the generated one is the one that cannot go stale.
